cues.zh: 哇，那些灯真亮。嗨，我叫 Ron Minnick。我在 Google 工作。

cues.en: And my talk today is about replacing your exploit written firmware with a Linux kernel.
cues.zh: 我今天的演讲是关于用 Linux 内核替换你写的漏洞固件。

cues.en: Now for the past ten years when I've talked about firmware,
cues.zh: 过去十年里，每当我谈到固件，

cues.en: people have gotten used to assuming I'm wearing my core boot hat, which is a core boot hat. It's a very nice hat.
cues.zh: 人们已经习惯性地以为我戴着 core boot 的帽子，这确实是顶 core boot 帽子。是顶很不错的帽子。

cues.en: I am not wearing my core boot hat today.
cues.zh: 今天我没戴我的 core boot 帽子。

cues.en: This is very much not a core boot talk.
cues.zh: 这绝对不是一场 core boot 演讲。

cues.zh: 我得提几位合作伙伴。

cues.en: Two are in the audience here today, Jean Marie Verdun, and I'm gonna slaughter the names with my terrible accent, and Guillaume, and we
cues.zh: 今天有两位在观众席，Jean Marie Verdun，我这糟糕的口音肯定要把名字念错了，还有 Guillaume，我们

cues.en: have several people working... Who've worked on this at Google, and then Trammell Hudson from two Cigna,
cues.zh: 有好几个人在……在 Google 参与了这个项目，还有来自 two Cigna 的 Trammell Hudson，

cues.en: who's been very important, and Andre Mirchowski at Cisco who helped a lot with the go part I'll describe in a bit.
cues.zh: 他非常重要，以及 Cisco 的 Andre Mirchowski，他在我稍后会讲到的 Go 部分帮了很大忙。

cues.en: Gonna start with the results. We had
cues.zh: 先从结果说起。我们

cues.en: a Facebook compute node, which I'm calling the o c p node, up in our booth.
cues.zh: 在我们的展台上放了一个 Facebook 计算节点，我称它为 o c p 节点。

cues.en: And we got the boot time from eight minutes to twenty seconds. And to be honest,
cues.zh: 我们把启动时间从八分钟缩短到了二十秒。说实话，

cues.en: to my way of thinking, that's the... Maybe the single least important part about this work.
cues.zh: 在我看来，这……也许是这项工作中最不重要的一部分。

cues.en: And you'll see why I'm saying that in a minute.
cues.zh: 你很快就会明白我为什么这么说。

cues.en: All the user land is written in Go, so we have a kernel and an init ram f s in flash
cues.zh: 所有用户态都是用 Go 写的，所以我们在闪存里有一个内核和一个 init ram f s

cues.en: and the user land for that init ram f s is all Go including init.
cues.zh: 而这个 init ram f s 的用户态全是 Go 写的，包括 init。

cues.en: This brings Linux performance reliability and I forgot to say security to firmware.
cues.zh: 这给固件带来了 Linux 的性能、可靠性，还有我忘了说的安全性。

cues.en: And key point of this, and you'll see what I mean by this in a minute, is we eliminate all of the UEFI and ME post boot activity.
cues.zh: 而这其中的关键点——一会儿你们就会明白我的意思——在于我们消除了所有 UEFI 和 ME 在引导之后的活动。

cues.en: Here's the problem.
cues.zh: 问题来了。

cues.en: When we began Linux, know, we all, you know, joined it in the nineties.
cues.zh: 当我们开始搞 Linux 的时候，你知道的，我们大家，你知道的，在九十年代加入了进来。

cues.en: It controlled everything about the x 86 platform. It was classic Intel five eighty six processor.
cues.zh: 它控制了 x86 平台的方方面面。那是经典的英特尔 586 处理器。

cues.en: But where we are today,
cues.zh: 但以我们今天的处境来看，

cues.en: between Linux and the hardware, there are at least two and a half kernels.
cues.zh: 在 Linux 和硬件之间，至少存在着两个半内核。

cues.en: And they are complete for proprietary
cues.zh: 而且它们完全是专有的，

cues.en: and not surprisingly based on that, they're exploit friendly.
cues.zh: 毫不奇怪的是，基于这一点，它们对漏洞利用（exploit）非常友好。

cues.en: It's pretty easy to write exploits for these other operating systems.
cues.zh: 为这些其他的操作系统编写漏洞利用程序相当容易。

cues.en: These run at a higher privilege level than Linux.
cues.zh: 这些东西运行在比 Linux 更高的特权级别上。

cues.en: They can control and manipulate Linux,
cues.zh: 它们可以控制和操纵 Linux，

cues.en: And those exploits can persist. So unlike the kind of exploits where you write, you know, something to the disk and we can always get out from under that by formatting the disk again,
cues.zh: 而且这些漏洞利用可以持久化。因此，不像那种你往磁盘里写入某种东西、然后我们总能通过重新格式化磁盘来摆脱它们的漏洞利用，

cues.en: these exploits can be placed in the operating... The the motherboard flash and you're never gonna get them out.
cues.zh: 这些漏洞利用可以被放置在操作系统的……主板闪存中，而你永远也无法清除它们。

cues.en: So once they're in there,
cues.zh: 所以一旦它们进去了，

cues.en: maybe one of your options is you shred your motherboard because there's just no other way out of the problem.
cues.zh: 你可能的一个选择就是把主板砸碎，因为实在没有别的办法来解决这个问题了。

cues.en: I used to give this talk
cues.zh: 我过去经常做这个演讲，

cues.en: and the title was if you trust your computer, you're crazy.
cues.zh: 标题是：如果你信任你的电脑，那你就是疯了。

cues.en: Fortunately, hopefully, I'm gonna talk about ways to deal with some of these problems
cues.zh: 幸运的是，希望如此，我接下来要谈谈如何应对其中一些问题的方法，

cues.en: so we can stop being crazy and maybe get a little sane.
cues.zh: 这样我们就能不再发疯，或许能变得稍微正常一点。

cues.en: So here are the operating systems and, you know, there's the one you're used to,
cues.zh: 所以这里有操作系统，你知道的，有你习惯的那种，

cues.en: which is ring zero Linux, and then there's ring minus one. We call that ring minus one. It's never really been ring minus one, but, basically, we kinda ran out of ring numbers. So fine. It's ring minus one. And so we've come to call the other two
cues.zh: 也就是环 0 的 Linux，然后还有环负一。我们把它叫作环负一。其实它从来都不是真正的环负一，但基本上，我们的环编号快用完了。好吧。那就叫环负一。所以我们把另外两个叫作

cues.en: ring minus two and ring minus three. The ring minus two kernel and half kernel
cues.zh: 环负二和环负三。环负二内核和半内核

cues.en: control everything about the CPU.
cues.zh: 掌控着关于 CPU 的一切。

cues.en: I call system managed mode a half kernel because it traps the eighty eighty six sixteen bit mode. Every time you close your lid or do certain other things on your Mac or on your laptop, it's probably trapping to eighty eighty six classic 16 bit mode. That should make you happy. Right? No protections at all in that mode. And then there's the UEFI kernel running in 64 bit page mode. And sometimes things trap the SMM and pop out in UEFI.
cues.zh: 我把系统管理模式称为半内核，因为它会捕获 8086 十六位模式。每次你合上笔记本盖子，或者在 Mac 或笔记本上执行某些其他操作时，它可能都在捕获经典的 8086 十六位模式。这应该会让你高兴。对吧？那个模式下没有任何保护。然后是在 64 位分页模式下运行的 UEFI 内核。有时有些东西会捕获 SMM 然后在 UEFI 中跳出来。

cues.en: So Linux isn't even running at that point.
cues.zh: 所以此时 Linux 甚至都没有在运行。

cues.en: And then there's ring minus three, and this is the one that has people really worried.
cues.zh: 然后是环负三，这个才是真正让人担心的。

cues.en: This is... There are three eighty eighty six CPUs on your die usually.
cues.zh: 这是……通常你的芯片晶圆上有三个 8086 CPU。

cues.en: One's called the management engine, and that's the one of concern.
cues.zh: 其中一个叫作管理引擎，这就是让人担心的那个。

cues.en: The other one is called the integrated sensor hub. We're not gonna worry about that today. And I don't know why. I really love the name of the other one. It's the innovation engine.
cues.zh: 另一个叫作集成传感器 hub。我们今天先不谈这个。而且我不知道为什么，我真的很喜欢另一个的名字。它叫作创新引擎。

cues.en: I just... Every time I say that, I kinda have to laugh a little. The ME, though, runs Minix three,
cues.zh: 我只是……每次我这么说，都忍不住有点想笑。不过 ME 运行的是 Minix 3，

cues.en: and that's why this is the year of Minix on the desktop. Because if you add up all the nodes running Windows and all the nodes running Linux, that's less than all the nodes running Minix three,
cues.zh: 所以今年是桌面上的 Minix 之年。因为把所有运行 Windows 的节点和所有运行 Linux 的节点加起来，还不如运行 Minix 3 的节点多，

cues.en: which, I guess, Andy Tannenbaum would like to know.
cues.zh: 我猜 Andy Tannenbaum 会想知道这一点。

cues.en: What's in ring minus two and ring minus three? IP stacks, and there's no common code between these as far as I can tell. File systems, drivers, DISNET, USB, and mouse. Why do you have to have file systems in the ME? Because it can reimage your node.
cues.zh: ring -2 和 ring -3 里有什么？IP 协议栈，而且据我所知，它们之间没有共用代码。文件系统、驱动、DISNET、USB 和鼠标。为什么 ME 里要有文件系统？因为它可以给你的节点重装镜像。

cues.en: Web servers, there's a web server in the ring minus three eighty eighty six running Minix. That was the result... You know, that was the, thing you might have read about a recent exploit with the zero length password giving you full admin access to your machine.
cues.zh: Web 服务器，ring -3 的 8086 里有一个运行 Minix 的 Web 服务器。这就是结果……你知道，这可能就是你读到过的最近那个漏洞：零长度密码让你获得机器的完整管理员权限。

cues.en: And, again, these things can reimage your workstation if it's turned off. If it's plugged into the wall and turned off and on a net, it'll get reimaged maybe without you knowing it.
cues.zh: 而且，这些东西能在你的工作站关机时给它重装镜像。如果它插着电源、处于关机状态并且连在网上，它可能会在你不知情的情况下被重装镜像。

cues.en: Here are some of the components of the management engine. I can't claim I know what all these do.
cues.zh: 这里是管理引擎的一些组件。我不能说我知道它们全都做什么。

cues.en: I can't claim to understand why there's full network manageability, regular network manageability and manageability.
cues.zh: 我不能说我理解为什么会有完整网络可管理性、常规网络可管理性，以及可管理性。

cues.en: I don't know why, you know, small business technology is in there. What small business technology meant originally about ten years ago is it's really inconvenient to set up passwords, so we just don't have a password for the ME.
cues.zh: 我不知道，你知道，为什么小型企业技术也在里面。大约十年前，小型企业技术最初的意思是：设置密码真的很不方便，所以我们干脆不给 ME 设密码。

cues.en: There's a thing in there called the outbreak containment heuristic.
cues.zh: 里面有个叫疫情遏制启发式的东西。

cues.en: I don't know if that comes from the movie.
cues.zh: 我不知道这是不是来自那部电影。

cues.en: And then the protected audio video path, which at least some people claim to me means DRM
cues.zh: 然后是受保护的音视频路径，至少有些人跟我说这意味着DRM

cues.en: for audio and video.
cues.zh: 用于音频和视频。

cues.en: Here is a great... And these slides are open, I'll mail them to you if you don't catch them. So don't worry about copying this. But Vasilis Severus about ten years ago did a fantastic master's thesis on ME flaws,
cues.zh: 这里有个很棒的……这些幻灯片是公开的，如果没跟上我会邮件发给你们。别担心抄这个。但Vasilis Severus大约十年前做了一篇关于ME漏洞的精彩硕士论文，

cues.en: and it was kinda depressing because basically everything could get attacked
cues.zh: 而且挺让人沮丧的，因为基本上一切都能被攻击

cues.en: and not all those have gotten fixed.
cues.zh: 而且并不是所有漏洞都修好了。

cues.en: So just for fun, can Google Intel ME exploit.
cues.zh: 所以纯属好玩，搜一下Google Intel ME exploit。

cues.en: 50,000,000 hits, I kind of enjoyed that. And the wired headline was pretty funny. Intel fixes a critical bug that lingered for seven dang years.
cues.zh: 5000万条结果，我还挺享受的。Wired的标题挺搞笑的。Intel修复了一个潜伏了整整七年的严重漏洞。

cues.en: You know, and if you do the math, that's kind of like kind of a billion machines.
cues.zh: 你算一下，那大概就是十亿台机器。

cues.en: And, you know, the fix is just reflash your firmware.
cues.zh: 而且修复办法就是重刷固件。

cues.en: Now how many people want to believe that a billion machines have been repatched since last spring with new firmware to fix this bug? I certainly don't believe it. I think... I'm sure that bug is still out there, and the web servers are still out there, and you can still send a lot of them a zero length password and have admin access.
cues.zh: 现在有多少人愿意相信自去年春天以来，十亿台机器都用新固件重新打过补丁来修这个漏洞？我肯定不信。我觉得……我确信那个漏洞还在，那些Web服务器也还在，你仍然可以给其中很多发一个零长度密码就拿到管理员权限。

cues.en: The Rig minus two half OS was originally used for power management. It came in with the four eighty six. Here's the problem. I have a laptop based on a four eighty six running DOS, and I closed the lid, and I wanted to sleep.
cues.zh: Rig minus two half OS最初是用于电源管理的。它随486一起出现。问题来了。我有台基于486跑DOS的笔记本，我合上盖子，想让它睡眠。

cues.en: DOS isn't gonna do that. And so what they did is add a very high privilege mode, higher privilege than ring zero that sort of can take over the machine when certain events happen. They're called system management interrupts,
cues.zh: DOS 不会那么做。所以他们做的是增加一个非常高特权的模式，比 ring 0 特权还高，在特定事件发生时能接管机器。它们叫系统管理中断，

cues.en: and that
cues.zh: 而那个

cues.en: stuff can take certain actions.
cues.zh: 东西能执行某些操作。

cues.en: And, you know, can't really go into all the details. It's a pretty long story, but all kinds of interrupts can go there. So if back in the day,
cues.zh: 而且，你知道，没法细讲。说来话长，但各种中断都能进到那里。所以以前，

cues.en: had a kernel that didn't support USB and you plugged the USB mouse in it and it worked, it's because of a full USB stack that exists in system management mode,
cues.zh: 如果你的内核不支持 USB，你插上 USB 鼠标它却能工作，那是因为系统管理模式里有一套完整的 USB 栈，

cues.en: independent of every other piece of code you've ever seen. And that's why sometimes maybe you'd plug a mouse in and it wouldn't work because USB stack didn't support that particular mouse.
cues.zh: 独立于你见过的其他所有代码。这也是为什么有时候你插上鼠标却不能用，因为那套 USB 栈不支持那个特定鼠标。

cues.en: Are there SMI exploits? Yeah. There are lot of SMI exploits. And
cues.zh: 有 SMI 漏洞利用吗？有。有很多 SMI 漏洞利用。而且

cues.en: the big problem with SMM is
cues.zh: SMM 的大问题是

cues.en: the the way in which it works is once enabled, you can't turn it off. As part of enabling it, you set a bit that essentially takes a big eight meg chunk of RAM and makes it invisible to every other operating mode.
cues.zh: 它的工作方式是：一旦启用，你就关不掉。启用过程中，你会设置一个位，基本上就是把一大块 8MB 的 RAM 藏起来，让其他所有运行模式都看不见。

cues.en: So it kinda... It's a cloaking device. Right? It just vanishes.
cues.zh: 所以它有点……像隐形装置。对吧？它直接消失了。

cues.en: This this memory with its stuff in it. So you kinda can't really know what it's gonna do. You can't disable it. You can't turn it off, and it's hidden. So it's a good way to maintain vendor control over you.
cues.zh: 这块内存连同里面的东西。所以你根本没法真正知道它会干什么。你不能禁用它。你不能关掉它，而且它是隐藏的。所以这是让厂商持续控制你的好办法。

cues.en: And finally, there's ring minus two, which is UEFI.
cues.zh: 最后还有负二环，也就是 UEFI。

cues.en: That runs on the main CPU along with SMM. This is an extremely complex kernel,
cues.zh: 它和 SMM 一样，运行在主 CPU 上。这是一个极其复杂的内核，

cues.en: and I think one source of the exploits is that a lot of people, let's say vendors, are writing against this kernel and don't really know all the rules, and they make mistakes.
cues.zh: 我认为漏洞利用的一个来源是，很多人，比如说硬件厂商，都在针对这个内核编写代码，却并不真正了解所有规则，因此犯下了错误。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: the result is that there are big giant holes that people can drive exploits through.
cues.zh: 结果就是出现了巨大的安全漏洞，攻击者可以利用这些漏洞实施攻击。

cues.en: For the most part, UEFI, from what I can tell the security model of sub security.
cues.zh: 据我所知，总体来说，UEFI 的安全模型在安全性方面存在不少问题。

cues.en: How many people here have written code for UEFI? I'm just curious.
cues.zh: 在座有多少人写过 UEFI 代码？我只是有点好奇。

cues.en: Oh, that is a lot.
cues.zh: 哦，人还真不少。

cues.en: Okay. Did you like it?
cues.zh: 好，你们觉得它好用吗？

cues.en: Okay. So I never liked it personally, but I'm just curious.
cues.zh: 好吧，我个人一直不喜欢它，不过还是有点好奇。

cues.en: Are there UEFI exploits? Oh my gosh. There are UEFI exploits.
cues.zh: UEFI 有漏洞利用案例吗？天哪，当然有。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: kind of the weird thing about UEFI, the model has always been that it's so darn smart
cues.zh: UEFI 有个相当奇怪的设计理念，它一直认为自己足够智能，

cues.en: that a kernel can sort of drop random bits of UEFI update into memory and then pull this chain and UEFI will update itself perfectly. There are no bugs in this process. And of course there are bugs because we all write code with bugs.
cues.zh: 以至于内核可以随意把 UEFI 更新的零散内容放进内存，然后触发一系列操作，UEFI 就能完美地完成自我更新。整个过程中不会出现任何 bug。当然，这怎么可能呢？毕竟我们写的代码都有 bug。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: the worry for me has always been that,
cues.zh: 我一直担心的是，

cues.en: you know, we get an exploited UEFI written, and then we go and say, hey. I don't like you, UEFI. Update yourself, but it's an unexploited UEFI, and it says, sure. I updated myself, but it doesn't.
cues.zh: 如果有人植入了恶意代码，攻陷了 UEFI，然后我们想说：“嘿，UEFI，我不喜欢你现在这个样子。更新一下自己。”我们提供的却是一个未被攻陷的 UEFI 版本。它会回答：“好的，我已经更新好了。”但实际上根本没有。

cues.en: So the worry has been that you can make an exploit that can't ever be removed. And again, the only remediation is a shredder.
cues.zh: 所以我一直担心，有人可能制造出一种永远无法清除的漏洞利用。再说一次，唯一的补救办法就是用碎纸机把设备彻底销毁。

cues.en: Here are some of the UEFI components. I... This is on the OCP node, which is a pretty limited node. I am told that there can be hundreds of these.
cues.zh: 这里是部分 UEFI 组件。我……这运行在 OCP 节点上，这是一个相当受限的节点。据我所知，这样的节点可能有数百个。

cues.en: And just look at some of this stuff. There's USB stack. There's an I p six and I p four protocol stuff.
cues.zh: 看看这些东西。有 USB 协议栈。还有 IPv6 和 IPv4 协议相关的东西。

cues.en: Has anybody here got a machine with an ISA bus? Just curious.
cues.zh: 这里有人有带 ISA 总线的机器吗？只是好奇。

cues.en: There's ISA bus support in case you find something from long ago.
cues.zh: 这里有 ISA 总线支持，以防你翻出什么年代久远的老古董。

cues.en: There's just a lot of stuff in there. IDE,
cues.zh: 里面东西太多了。IDE、

cues.en: you know, and all this stuff is pulling IO driven. It's got
cues.zh: 你知道的，所有这些东西都是由 I/O 驱动的。它有

cues.en: lots of delays built in. Okay? It's very, very primitive drivers,
cues.zh: 内置了大量的延迟。好吗？驱动程序非常非常原始，

cues.en: and that's one reason it's so slow to boot.
cues.zh: 这也是它启动如此慢的原因之一。

cues.en: So we've got these two and a half hidden OSs.
cues.zh: 所以我们有这隐蔽的两个半操作系统。

cues.en: They have a lot of capabilities. They have network stacks and web servers.
cues.zh: 它们有很多能力，比如网络栈和 Web 服务器。

cues.en: They implement self modifying code that can persist across power cycles
cues.zh: 它们实现了能够在断电后持久保存的自修改代码

cues.en: And and the goal here is to reduce the scope of the two and a half OSs. And I will say that a lot of what we're doing here will apply to AMD processors, just not the management engine parts.

cues.en: This project is called NERF.
cues.zh: 这个项目叫 NERF。

cues.en: UEFI stands for Unified Extensible Firmware Interface. We consider extensibility harmful, so NERF stands for non extensible reduced firmware.
cues.zh: UEFI 全称是统一可扩展固件接口。我们认为可扩展性是有害的，所以 NERF 代表的是不可扩展精简固件。

cues.en: The goal is you make firmware less capable of doing harm. You make the things it does do very visible. We get rid of all those runtime components in the management engine in UEFI.
cues.zh: 目标是让固件没那么大能力干坏事，让它做的事情非常透明。我们去掉管理引擎和 UEFI 里所有那些运行时组件。

cues.en: And in particular, we're... You know, it's hard to kill everything the ME does. Your node won't turn on in many cases, but we did take away its web server and IP stack. Good thing to do in my opinion.

cues.en: And we also removed the UEFI IP stack and other drivers it might have. So... And finally, we removed their ability to reflash themselves. We don't want them doing that, so they don't.
cues.zh: 我们还移除了 UEFI 的 IP 协议栈和其他可能有的驱动。所以……最后，我们移除了它们自我刷写的能力。我们不希望它们那么做，所以它们就做不了了。

cues.en: So we don't want the ME at all. You can't get rid of the ME. It's on the die. ME The is the first thing that turns on when you turn on the chip. The ME starts all the clocks up. cues.zh: 我们根本不想要 ME。但你摆脱不了 ME。它在芯片裸片上。ME 是芯片一上电最先启动的东西。ME 启动所有时钟。在较新的处理器上，有一个复位向量。主 CPU 会取它。很多情况下，是 ME 把这个向量提供给 CPU。

cues.en: It's there for good.

cues.zh: 很多情况下，它会开机，然后在三十分钟后自动关机。背后的逻辑是，ME 认为固件有问题：我给你三十分钟修复，然后我就关机。

好吧。所以，你知道的，你真的是、真的无法干掉它。
